column1: # Registry of REDACTED FIGURES — consumed by scripts/corrections_inventory.sh (2026-09-26).
# WHY THIS IS NOT A ROW IN WITHDRAWN_FIGURES.tsv OR RETRACTED_FIGURES.tsv
#   Those registries list a withdrawn figure as a FIXED string, and the published text may keep
#   it next to a supersession marker. The figures here are a different class: a report withdrew
#   them AND redacted them, on TR-12 §9's rule that a correction which requotes a number
#   publishes it (TR-11 v1.10 did the same to its own changelog row). Listing one here as a
#   fixed string would restate it. So each row is the sha256 of the figure, not the figure.
#   This hides nothing: the figures stand in public commit messages, and a short dollar string
#   can be recovered from its digest by trial. The point is only that no current file restates
#   them.
# WHAT READS IT
#   scripts/corrections_inventory.sh takes every dollar-figure token from the text it sweeps
#   (a dollar sign, a number, an optional K or M, an optional dash and second number; trailing
#   full stops and commas dropped), hashes it, and writes "[withdrawn figure redacted]" in the
#   text column of documentation/CORRECTIONS_INVENTORY.tsv wherever the digest is listed here.
#   The row id is computed before the redaction, so no published id changes.
# SCOPE: only cost figures a report has withdrawn and redacted. A figure that was withdrawn but
# may still be quoted beside a marker belongs in WITHDRAWN_FIGURES.tsv, not here.
# FORMAT (tab-separated, 2 columns). Each dash spelling is its own row.
#   <sha256 of the figure, UTF-8, no newline>
